claims.claim: Spring Boot fits in 512 MB if configured with care
claims.measured: java-spring peak memory 220–500 MB across tests in a 512 MB container (499 MB on single-row DB, 500 MB on 20-query DB); java-spring-vt 209–444 MB
claims.why: Spring Boot completed every test inside a 512 MB container, but it peaked at about 500 MB, so 'with care' is a fair warning.

claims.claim: Go, Node.js or Rust use less memory than the Spring Boot stack
claims.measured: Go 7–16 MB, Rust 3–10 MB, Node 55–77 MB peak vs java-spring 220–500 MB peak; idle 1–43 MB vs 134 MB
claims.why: All three use much less memory than Spring Boot in every test, so the claim points the right way.

claims.claim: A simple 'parse JSON and insert one row' request on warmed-up Java should use well under 5 ms of CPU
claims.measured: java-spring single-row DB 7,668 req/s at 100% of 1 CPU (~0.13 ms CPU/request); java-spring-vt 12,731 req/s; JSON 27,264 req/s
claims.why: The measured cost is about 0.1–0.15 ms of CPU per request, which is well under 5 ms.

claims.claim: At 200 requests/s one Spring Boot instance on one CPU might cope, but without much spare room
claims.measured: java-spring 7,668 req/s single-row DB, 1,254 req/s even with 20 queries per request, on 1 CPU
claims.why: One CPU handled about 38 times the stated peak for a one-row query, and over 6 times it with 20 queries per request, so headroom is large, not small.

claims.claim: Expect Spring Boot start-up on one CPU to take from several seconds to tens of seconds
claims.why: The measured ~6 s start-up is 'several seconds', the low end of the claimed range.

claims.claim: Expect the first minutes to be slower while Java optimises the code
claims.why: The benchmark leaves out a 5 s warm-up and does not report performance during warm-up.

claims.claim: Newer Java versions (Java 25) use less memory per object and start faster
claims.why: The measurements do not compare Java versions.

claims.claim: Plain JDBC uses less memory and CPU per request than JPA/Hibernate
claims.why: The benchmark does not say which data-access layer Spring used and does not compare JDBC with JPA.

claims.claim: Quarkus or Micronaut have lower memory use and faster startup than Spring Boot
claims.why: Neither Quarkus nor Micronaut was measured.

claims.claim: GraalVM native image gives much less memory and almost instant startup
claims.why: No native-image Java server was measured.

claims.claim: By default Java gives itself only a quarter of RAM (about 128 MB) on a 512 MB machine
claims.why: The measurements report total peak memory, not JVM heap settings.
